title: SNAP participation is not a like-for-like person-rate comparison
evidence: c80b6c4:data/comparison.json, SNAP/US/total rows: eligible_count is held_out; participation_rate is consumed_as_target through FNS average-month household counts, not a direct person target.

pipeline/compute_counterparts.py:300-306 maps the SPM-unit annual SNAP amount and eligibility result to every person, so it counts all SPM-unit members rather than identified SNAP assistance-unit members.
PEUS@92e6052d3e:policyengine_us/variables/gov/usda/snap/snap.py:4-35 defines monthly SNAP at SPM-unit level and applies an annual SPM-unit take-up flag.

POP@8828dee:tools/build_us_target_parity_manifest.py:179-198 says the FNS person indicator overcounts by about 50% in PE because the model lacks sub-unit participation; the calibrated counterpart is the household caseload.
POP@8828dee:packages/populace-build/tests/test_us_fiscal_targets.py:1130-1149 deliberately excludes FNS average-month person targets until sub-unit participation is modeled.

USDA FNS SNAP Monthly State Participation and Benefit Summary FY69 to Current, US Summary row 21 column C: 42,176,946.1667 average-month persons in FY2023 and 41,690,237.75 in FY2024; LEDGER:tests/test_ledger_source_package.py:2932-3006 verifies the FY2024 series.
docs/replication-assessment.md:38-60,64-78,130-135 distinguishes Urban's 2023 average-month caseload from PE's annual 2024 construction and Build P's household-count calibration.
quantification: PE reports 60.462M mapped participant persons / 66.364M annual eligible persons = 91.107%; Urban reports 57.5% and a rounded 29.361M gap. Dividing FNS average-month persons by PE's annual eligible pool gives 63.55% for FY2023 and 62.82% for FY2024. That substitution removes 27.55-28.29 percentage points, or 82.0-84.2% of the published 33.61-point rate difference, leaving 6.05 points (FY2023) or 5.32 points (FY2024). PE's mapped participant count is 43.4-45.0% above FNS, while Urban's participant count inferred from its rounded gap is 4.6-5.7% below FNS. PE eligibility is only 4.0% below Urban.

fix_draft.title: SNAP person rates mix annual SPM-unit membership with average-month FNS persons
fix_draft.body: PolicyEngine's 91.1% is a derived annual person statistic: every person in an SPM unit with positive 2024 SNAP is counted. Build P consumes USDA FNS average-month household targets, so household agreement is calibration-by-construction; FNS person targets are deliberately excluded because PE does not model within-SPM SNAP assistance-unit membership. FNS FY2023/FY2024 average-month persons divided by PE's annual eligible pool imply 63.6%/62.8%, leaving 6.1/5.3 percentage points relative to Urban's 57.5%. Do not present 91.1% and 57.5% as like-for-like rates.

open_questions: Why does Urban's participant count inferred from its rounded gap sit 1.92-2.41M below the FNS FY2024/FY2023 national person series?
How much of the remaining difference comes from average-month eligibility versus PE's annual eligible pool?
Should PE model SNAP assistance-unit membership instead of mapping the SPM-unit flag to all members?

POP@8828dee:packages/populace-build/src/populace/build/us/take_up_contract.json:30-45 seeds TANF at 0.219 but states that no ASEC PAW receipt anchor is threaded through the base spine.

PEUS@92e6052d3e TX tx_tanf_income_eligible.py:14-40, IN in_tanf_countable_income_eligible.py:17-44, and DE de_tanf_net_income_eligible.py:12-28 branch on is_tanf_enrolled, so forced take-up still uses applicant rules when that input is false.

fix_draft.title: Thread TANF enrollment and add ACF caseload constraints before publishing payable eligibility
fix_draft.body: Build P seeds takes_up_tanf_if_eligible but does not thread a TANF/public-assistance receipt anchor into is_tanf_enrolled. In PE-US 1.764.6 that input defaults false, so forced take-up continues to run applicant branches in states such as TX, IN, and DE. Add a documented ASEC PAW/receipt mapping with ambiguity handling; expose a national positive-under-forced payable-eligibility variable; compile ACF average-month family and recipient count validations; add state forced-payable and dollar diagnostics; and investigate DE/IN/TX near-zero support plus NY over-support. Require the national consumed cash target and state caseload checks to pass before treating TANF rates as publishable.

open_questions: How does ATTIS assign current-recipient continuation rules, child-only cases, nonrecipient parents, and SSF programs?
Which ACF family or recipient series exactly matches Urban's numerator?
How much of the DE/IN/TX collapse comes from enrollment/applicant branching versus asset, income, or vehicle inputs?
Why does NY exceed Urban by 0.936M while many states undercount?

fix_draft.title: Reconcile ATTIS EITC eligibility to SOI claims and the NTA eligible universe
fix_draft.body: ATTIS reports 18.445M eligible tax units, 22% below the SOI claim count and 4.6-7.6M below the published TY2016 NTA/Treasury eligible-universe range. PE's forced count is held out, not a calibration target.

open_questions: Which ATTIS gates account for the 5.247M shortfall below SOI claims?
How much can erroneous or ineligible claiming explain?

Does PE's demographic test overcount adult-dependent edge cases because it evaluates the childless age rule across all tax-unit members?

fix_draft.title: Refundable CTC: PE is claims-shaped, while Urban is modeled eligibility
fix_draft.body: PolicyEngine counts tax units with positive baseline refundable_ctc. Because PE has no ACTC take-up/filer flag and the release weights consume IRS SOI ACTC claim-count and dollar targets, this count is claims-shaped rather than an independent estimate of statutory eligibility. Urban reports ATTIS-simulated eligibility. The roughly 5.9M difference therefore compares claims with modeled eligibles; claims may include erroneous or ineligible returns, and ATTIS may use a narrower filing construction. Add a forced-filing statutory ACTC eligibility metric before making a same-concept comparison, and correct the generated consumer-fact period label that calls 22incd.csv TY2023.

fix_draft.title: Validate SSI payable eligibility and recipient composition in finer adult age bands
fix_draft.body: Build P reports 9.99M payable-under-forced SSI adults versus ATTIS's 12.60M, but its sharper failure is age composition: +55% ages 18-24 and -85% ages 60-64. The release can pass because SSA controls pool every adult 18-64, while the SIPP disability imputation has only 577 positive training records, applies a hard measured-disability-signal gate, and is checked only at an aggregate level. Add component diagnostics for ABD/disability, resources, income, and immigration by 18-24, 25-59, 60-64, and 65+; add a held-out age-shape gate and regression fixtures; and document federal-payment payable eligibility separately from state SSP and essential-person concepts. open_questions: Which detailed-age administrative series supplies Urban's subgroup numerators?

Which PE component causes the 60-64 collapse: latent disability, SGA, resources, countable income, or immigration?

fix_draft.title: Full-participation poverty counterfactuals are not program- or period-matched

title: Alaska SNAP exposes post-calibration household-to-person saturation
evidence: c80b6c4:data/comparison.json, Alaska SNAP: eligible_count is held_out; participation_rate is consumed_as_target through FNS state average-month household counts. A divergence on the consumed quantity is therefore a calibration-machinery finding.

Build P us_snap_state_take_up.json: the pre-calibration Alaska FY2024 target is 31,319.25 households, eligible weight 33,205.856, caseload 31,109.222, and saturated=false; the diagnostic explicitly uses pre-calibration design weights.

Build P calibration_diagnostics.json, usda_snap.fy2024.state_average_monthly_households.wro.ak.average_monthly_households@2024: 31,319.25 target versus 31,325.745 final (+0.0207%), so the official household target is internally consistent and hit.

POP@8828dee:packages/populace-build/src/populace/build/us_runtime/snap_state_take_up.py:186-211 derives target / weighted eligible and clips at one; lines 307-380 define saturation and document pre-calibration weights.

POP@8828dee:packages/populace-build/src/populace/build/us/source_stages.json:1806 states that saturated states set all eligible units to take-up and that person targets are deliberately absent because SPM-unit membership overcounts SNAP assistance-unit participants.
pipeline/compute_counterparts.py:300-306 nevertheless maps SPM-unit receipt and eligibility to every person for the scorecard.
c80b6c4:data/comparison.json, state SNAP total rows: 15 jurisdictions are exactly 100%; 18 are at least 99.9% after adding AK, SD, and TX.
quantification: AK has 107,166.399 PE eligible persons, 107,163.924 mapped participant persons, a 99.99769% rate, and a 2.476-person gap; Urban reports 86,000 eligible, 34.2%, and about 57,000 gap. The FY2024 FNS Alaska household target is hit within 6.495 households (0.0207%), yet the person statistic nearly saturates. Fifteen jurisdictions are exactly 100% (AL, AR, DC, HI, ID, IN, LA, MS, MO, ND, OK, RI, TN, UT, WY); AK, SD, and TX bring the >=99.9% count to 18. The release-stage pre-calibration diagnostic marks 30 states saturated but marks AK false, whereas AK's final-weight person rate is 99.998%; this establishes that the current stage diagnostic does not describe the final-weight person result, but post-calibration eligible-unit weights are still needed to identify AK's exact causal path.

fix_draft.title: Stop SNAP state saturation from passing release and publish a person-compatible validation
fix_draft.body: Build P accepts target-at-or-above-eligible SPM-unit weight as saturation, and its stage diagnostic uses pre-calibration weights. AK nevertheless ships as 99.998% of eligible persons although its FY2024 FNS household target is hit within 0.021%; the pre-calibration diagnostic itself marks AK unsaturated. title: WIC validates the national level but exposes offsetting held-out age errors
evidence: c80b6c4:data/comparison.json, WIC national total and age rows: every eligible and participation quantity is held_out; calibration_basis says zero WIC calibration targets and identifies the match as out-of-sample.

POP@8828dee:packages/populace-build/src/populace/build/us/target_parity_manifest.json:680-689 excludes WIC targets; docs/mechanics-audit.md:200-205 and docs/replication-assessment.md:64-68 confirm the zero-target surface.

c80b6c4:data/comparison.json WIC age rows: infant eligibility is 1.394M PE vs 1.829M Urban; age 1-4 is 7.973M vs 7.616M. Rates are 81.520% vs 79.9% and 46.148% vs 47.2%, respectively.
quantification: National eligibility is 9,367,299 PE versus 9,444,000 Urban (-76,701, -0.812%); participation is 51.412% versus 53.5% (-2.088 points); the gap is 4,551,354 versus 4,389,000 (+162,354). fix_draft.title: Preserve the WIC holdout and diagnose the infant/child eligibility offset
fix_draft.body: Build P has zero WIC calibration targets, so Urban's national 2023 totals are held-out and independently recomputed. National eligibility agrees within 0.8%, but that total hides a 435k (23.8%) infant shortfall offset by 357k (4.7%) more children ages 1-4. Add held-out age and state diagnostics, beginning with the populace#520 infant-geography concern; preserve a validation holdout or target rotation before adding WIC controls. Continue to label participation as source-seeded from FNS CY2022 category rates, not an unanchored forecast or a consumed calibration target.
